title: Company-wide policies and processes: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement, vendor management, travel, templates
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview:
This document centralizes Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees, managers, and process owners.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and temporary staff across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Covers corporate systems, production and non-production environments, cloud accounts, vendor relationships, and company-funded travel and procurement.
- Does not replace team-level runbooks; teams must align local procedures with these standards.

Key principles:
- Least privilege: grant the minimum access necessary and review periodically.
- Separation of duties: critical actions require dual controls or approval chains.
- Auditability: all changes and approvals must be auditable in the designated systems.
- Cost-consciousness: procurement decisions should balance cost, reliability, and compliance.
- Data protection: classify and treat data consistently with legal and regulatory obligations.

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose: Ensure secure, least-privilege access to company and customer resources.
Owner: Security (policy) / People Ops (onboarding and offboarding processes)

Access lifecycle:
1. Request: Employees request access via our IAM portal (AccessHub). Requests must include justification, duration, and owner.
2. Approval: Managers approve for standard resource access. For elevated or sensitive data access, Security and the resource owner must approve.
3. Provision: Automation grants access where available; manual steps are documented in the resource owner's onboarding checklist.
4. Review: Quarterly access review for all privileged groups; ad-hoc review for terminated or role-changed employees.
5. Revoke: Access is revoked immediately on termination or when no longer required.

Roles and responsibilities:
- People Ops: initiate onboarding/offboarding workflows and escalate exceptions.
- Managers: verify business justification and approve role-based access.
- Resource owners: maintain the list of eligible approvers and periodic review cadence.
- Security: approve access to sensitive systems and maintain IAM policies.

Access levels and examples:
- Standard employee: email, VPN (conditional), internal docs, non-prod systems.
- Privileged: production deploy, production DB read/write, key management console. Requires 2 approvers and periodic certification.
- Sensitive-data access: PII, customer data, or audit logs. Requires Security + Data Owner approval and MFA enforced.

Exceptions:
- Temporary elevated access must include start/end date and ticket in the ticketing system (TICK-xxxxx). Maximum 30 days unless extended with Security approval.

2) Change Management
Purpose: Reduce risk from infrastructure and application changes while enabling rapid delivery.
Owner: Eng Platform / Eng SRE

Change categories and approval matrix:
- Standard Changes (pre-authorized): routine, low-risk (e.g., certificate renewals, small config updates) - no CAB required; implement during maintenance windows.
- Normal Changes: require change request (CR) in ChangeTracker, impact assessment, and approval by the service owner and SRE on call. CAB (weekly) approval if the change impacts multiple services.
- Emergency Changes: must be documented as Emergency CR, implemented by senior engineer with SRE approval, and retro-reviewed within 48 hours.

Change procedure (normal changes):
1. Create CR in ChangeTracker with description, rollback plan, test plan, and owners.
2. Impact analysis and risk scoring (low/med/high).
3. Obtain approvals: Service Owner -> SRE -> CAB (if cross-service or high risk).
4. Schedule in the change calendar; notify stakeholders 48 hours prior.
5. Execute in the approved window; follow runbook and automated checks.
6. Post-change verification and update documentation.
7. Post-implementation review for high-risk or failed changes.

Emergency change checklist:
- Record the incident ticket and link to CR.
- Notify on-call SRE and Security if customer data may be affected.
- After stabilization, produce a postmortem and schedule for CAB review.

3) Data Management
Purpose: Ensure data is classified, stored, retained, and disposed in compliance with legal and operational needs.
Owner: Security (policy) / Data Stewards (operational)

Data classification:
- Public: safe for public disclosure.
- Internal: company-internal information with no customer PII.
- Confidential: contains business-sensitive material (financials, roadmap).
- Restricted: PII, customer data, or regulated datasets.

Handling rules by classification:
- Public: stored on public channels or web. No special controls.
- Internal: access monitored; standard backups.
- Confidential: encrypted at rest; access limited to business need; retained for minimum of 2 years unless business justification.
- Restricted: encryption in transit and at rest, strict RBAC, logged access, retention and deletion policies defined per contract.

Retention and deletion:
- Default retention: production logs - 180 days; cost-sensitive logs - 30 days on hot storage, 365 days on archive.
- Customer datasets: retain per contract; Data Stewards maintain catalog with retention rules.
- Deletion: use Data Deletion Request (DDR) process; Security and Legal must approve for restricted datasets.

Backups and disaster recovery:
- Production backups: nightly snapshots with 30-day rolling retention on warm storage; critical datasets archived to cold storage quarterly.
- Restore drills: quarterly for critical services, annually for non-critical services; documented in DR playbook.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Purpose: Standardize purchasing, approvals, and expense reimbursement to control spend and ensure compliance.
Owner: Finance & Legal / People Ops (travel)

Procurement thresholds and approval matrix:
- < $2,500 (direct spend): Manager approval in procurement portal.
- $2,500 - $50,000: Director approval + finance notification.
- > $50,000: VP approval + Legal review and contract.
- Cloud spend commitments (reserved capacity): Sales/Finance negotiation; standard contract review by Legal.

Procurement process (software/hardware):
1. Submit Purchase Request in ProcurementPortal with business justification, vendor, estimated cost, and budget code.
2. Finance validates budget and issues PO after approvals.
3. Vendor receives PO; invoice routed to AP with PO reference.
4. Asset tagging: all hardware must be tagged by Asset Management upon receipt.

Expense reimbursement:
- Use ExpenseTracker for all reimbursements within 30 days of expense. Attach receipts.
- Travel: pre-approval required via TravelApproval; per diem table in Travel Policy section.
- Non-compliant expenses may be denied; repeated violations escalated to People Ops.

5) Vendor Management
Purpose: Ensure vendors are evaluated, onboarded, and monitored for performance, security, and contract compliance.
Owner: Finance & Legal / Vendor Manager

Vendor onboarding checklist:
1. Business case and cost estimate.
2. Legal review of contract (terms, data processing addendum if applicable).
3. Security assessment (questionnaire + risk scoring); high-risk vendors require SOC2/ISO evidence and a remediation plan.
4. Approvals: Procurement -> Finance -> Legal -> Security (for data access).
5. Add to vendor registry with owner, SLAs, and renewal dates.

Ongoing vendor governance:
- Quarterly vendor performance reviews for strategic or high-spend vendors.
- Annual security reassessment for vendors with access to sensitive data.
- Contract renewals: begin negotiation 90 days prior to renewal date; update registry.

SLA and incident expectations:
- Vendors must provide point of contact and escalation path in the contract.
- Security incidents involving vendor systems must be reported within 24 hours to Redwood Security.

6) Travel Policy (summary)
Purpose: Provide guidelines for business travel booking, safety, and reimbursement.
Owner: People Ops

Booking and approvals:
- All travel must be pre-approved in TravelApproval with purpose, dates, and estimated cost.
- Manager approval required; international travel also requires People Ops approval.
- Use approved travel vendors or the company travel portal for bookings - exceptions require justification.

Per diem and expenses:
- Domestic per diem: $75/day for meals and incidental expenses.
- International per diem: per country rates published in TravelApproval.
- Ground transportation: use rideshares or economy car rentals; upgrade with manager approval.
- Lodging: book standard rooms; exceptions documented.

Safety and insurance:
- Company travel insurance covers approved trips; register international travel with People Ops.
- In case of emergency, contact the Emergency Travel Hotline listed in People Ops resources.

7) Internal Templates and Required Artefacts
Purpose: Standardize documentation to reduce friction and improve auditability.
Owner: People Ops / Finance / Security (templates by domain)

Available templates (links are internal confluence pages):
- Purchase Request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/purchase-request
- Vendor Security Questionnaire template: /confluence/security-and-compliance/templates/vendor-sq
- Change Request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/change-request-template
- Access Request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/access-request
- Travel Approval template: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/travel-approval
- Incident / Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template

Template usage guidance:
- Always attach a completed template to the corresponding system ticket (ProcurementPortal, ChangeTracker, AccessHub).
- Use the latest published template; outdated templates are archived and listed on the templates index.

Governance and review cadence:
- People Ops maintains this central policy document and templates index.
- Security, Finance, and Legal must review and approve changes to their domain policies annually.
- Ad-hoc policy updates may occur for regulatory reasons; stakeholders are notified two weeks prior to enforcement.

Enforcement and exceptions:
- Non-compliance is handled via managerial coaching; repeat or serious violations escalate to HR and Legal.
- Exceptions require documented justification, an approval chain, and, where relevant, compensating controls.

Appendices:
A. Approval matrix (summary table):
| Action | Approver 1 | Approver 2 | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Hardware purchase <$2.5k | Manager | - | ProcPortal entry |
| Software subscription $5k-$50k | Director | Finance | Contract review if >$25k |
| Production DB schema change | Service Owner | SRE | CAB if cross-service |
| Access to restricted data | Manager | Security + Data Owner | Quarterly certification |

B. Useful links:
- AccessHub (IAM): internal://accesshub
- ChangeTracker: internal://changetracker
- ProcurementPortal: internal://procurement
- Vendor Registry: internal://vendor-registry
- Templates Index: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates-index

Contact and escalation:
- People Ops: people-ops@redwoodinference.com
- Security (policy queries): security-policy@redwoodinference.com
- Procurement/Finance: procurement@redwoodinference.com

Revision history:
- 2026-03-04: Initial consolidated policy created.
- 2026-12-01: Annual review - updated procurement thresholds, clarified emergency change retro-review window.

This document is the authoritative company-wide policy reference. For team-level runbooks or operational playbooks, see the relevant team space and align with the standards set here.
